name: BentoGrid
description: A responsive grid of feature cards of different sizes. It is a real list: each BentoCard is a list item with its own heading, icon, description, optional background and optional link or action. Cards lift a little on hover.

label.description: Accessible name of the list. Leave it out when a nearby heading already names the section and pass aria-labelledby instead.

isStill.description: Turns off the hover lift and its transition.

keyboard: Tab: moves to the link or button of each card in reading order
Enter: follows the link; Enter or Space presses the button
requirements: The grid is a ul and each BentoCard an li, so the number of cards is announced
Each card title is a real heading; set headingLevel on the cards to fit the page outline
The icon and the background slot are decoration and are hidden from assistive technology
A card with a link or action is operated by that one control, whose area covers the whole card; the card never has two tab stops
The hover lift is off for prefers-reduced-motion, inside rdm-still and with isStill, and only runs where there is a real pointer
On phones the cards stack in one column; from the medium breakpoint they use three columns, and column and row spans apply there
Real text in the server HTML; readable with no JavaScript
screenReader: List with the number of items, then each card: heading, description, then the link or button name

use_when: A feature overview with a few cards that deserve different emphasis
A landing page section of capabilities
avoid_when: Data that must be compared row by row (use a table)
Long lists of equal items (use a plain list or cards in a regular grid)
anti_patterns: Putting several links inside one card
Using spans so large that the grid leaves holes
